title: Choose Stif's visual world
question: The roll assigned the line network. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Line network
options.lineage: Paris métro wayfinding: enamel station plaques, line roundels, glazed white tile
options.thesis: Every list is a line with its own color and roundel, and every shared link transfers to its line by itself.
materials: a wayfinding sans (Signika, with its light-on-dark grade for night)
options.viewport: A tile-registered two-column board under a station-sign search bar; a row of line roundels filters it; each card wears its line's badge and a thin line-color edge.
options.risk: Can tip into transit pastiche: roundels must always do a job (filter, file, locate) and no transit logo or operator name ever appears.

raised.raise: A link resolves in place: title and price drop into fixed cells while the card keeps its size, so the board never reflows.
Product images are registered: one ratio, one ground, one scale across a list, so items compare at a glance.
Cards use one text size; a title is the body set heavier, so a hundred cards stay calm.
Done is a stamp, not a disappearance: bought, watched or visited links are punched and kept at the foot of their line.
Only content carries full color (images and roundels); chrome never floods a card.

options.label: Sorting rack
options.lineage: Post-office sorting cabinets: pigeonholes, destination labels, the dead-letter tray
options.thesis: Every link drops through one slot and lands in its pigeonhole; the board is a rack of labeled compartments.
options.viewport: A grid of compartments, one per list, each showing its newest items; a slot bar on top takes a link.
options.risk: Filing metaphors are where note apps usually land; it can read as folders in a costume.

options.label: Developer console
options.lineage: dark-first developer tools: graphite panels, hairline seams, syntax accents
options.thesis: Notes as persistent panels on graphite, labels in syntax colors, destructive actions isolated by empty space.
options.viewport: A dense panel list of notes with tabular metadata and a command-style capture bar.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and speaks your daily screen language, but a shopping list or a restaurant shortlist reads like a log file.
options.risk: The predictable choice for a developer's own tool; loses warmth for life admin.

options.label: Split-flap concourse board
options.thesis: Links as departure rows whose flaps cascade from 'reading…' to title, price and destination list.
options.viewport: A departures table of links with a destination column per list.
options.case: Fixed character cells fit link rows but not free-form notes; the métro world covers more of the product.
options.kept: In-place change: a resolving link updates its own cells without reflowing anything.
options.risk: A table for everything; text notes do not fit.

options.label: Botanical folio
options.thesis: Each note a fixed-scale plate on one shared baseline.
options.viewport: Banded plates with engraved italic titles.
options.case: Cream and italic serif is the default look for this kind of app, and it is not your world.
options.kept: Registration: every product image in a list shares one ratio, ground and scale.
options.risk: Generic-tasteful, the opposite of what you asked for.

options.label: Streaming title wall
options.thesis: Each URL list as a row of artwork tiles; the focused tile expands to show price and summary.
options.viewport: Rows of link images per list, text notes as plain tiles.
options.case: Strong for the link lists, weak for text notes and checklists, which make poor posters.
options.kept: Only content carries full color; chrome stays neutral.
options.risk: Turns a notebook into a media browser.

options.label: Airline timetable rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size everywhere; rank carried by weight, case and rule.
options.viewport: Raked slides of notes on a lit bed.
options.case: The raked layout fights reading and writing notes every day.
options.kept: One text size on cards; weight, not scale, makes the title.

options.label: Jet-age ticket wallet
options.lineage: airline coupon books and baggage tags
options.thesis: Lists as coupon books; items stamp themselves used or void instead of disappearing.
options.viewport: A wallet of tabbed coupons, one per list.
options.case: A rich state vocabulary, but the coupon shape suits checklists and links, not free text.
options.kept: Done is a stamp: completed items stay readable, marked, at the foot of their list.
options.risk: Vintage costume over a daily tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Keep's board done right: Material You colors, masonry cards, a take-a-note bar and a FAB.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar on top, masonry of pastel note cards, bottom bar with quick actions and a FAB.
canonCard.risk: Looks like Keep, which is the app being replaced.
